title: Work, Energy and Power — 40 MCQs
description: Covers work done by constant and variable forces, work-energy theorem, kinetic and potential energy formulae, conservation of energy, conservative and non-conservative forces, elastic and inelastic collisions in one dimension, and related numerical and conceptual problems.

questions.q: Work done by a constant force F when its point of application is displaced by s is given by
questions.explanation: Work is the scalar (dot) product W = F · s = F s cosθ, where θ is the angle between force and displacement.

questions.q: The SI unit of work is
questions.explanation: One joule is the work done by a force of 1 N acting through a displacement of 1 m in the direction of the force.

questions.q: Kinetic energy of a body of mass m moving with speed v is
questions.explanation: By definition K = ½ m v². It is a scalar quantity and is always non-negative.

questions.q: Gravitational potential energy of a mass m raised through a height h near the Earth’s surface is
questions.explanation: U = m g h, taking the zero of potential energy at the reference level from which h is measured.

questions.q: The work-energy theorem states that the work done by the net force on a particle equals
options: the change in its potential energy
the change in its kinetic energy
the change in its total mechanical energy
questions.explanation: W_net = ΔK = K_f − K_i. This follows directly from Newton’s second law integrated with respect to displacement.

questions.q: A force is said to be conservative if the work done by it
options: is independent of the path and depends only on the end points
questions.explanation: For a conservative force the work between two points is path-independent and equals the negative of the change in potential energy.

questions.q: In an elastic collision
options: both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved
neither momentum nor kinetic energy is conserved
questions.explanation: By definition an elastic collision conserves both linear momentum and kinetic energy.

questions.q: Power is defined as
questions.explanation: Average power P = W / Δt; instantaneous power P = F · v.

questions.q: The SI unit of power is
questions.explanation: One watt equals one joule per second.

questions.q: When a body is lifted slowly at constant speed, the work done by the lifting force equals
options: the change in gravitational potential energy
questions.explanation: At constant speed ΔK = 0, so the work done by the applied force equals the increase in gravitational PE.

questions.q: Friction is an example of a
questions.explanation: Work done against friction depends on the path length and is dissipated as heat; hence friction is non-conservative.

questions.q: In an inelastic collision
options: kinetic energy is conserved but momentum is not
momentum is conserved but kinetic energy is not
questions.explanation: Linear momentum is always conserved in the absence of external forces, but kinetic energy is not conserved in an inelastic collision.

questions.q: Work done by a variable force F(x) in moving a particle from x1 to x2 is
options: ∫ F dx from x1 to x2
questions.explanation: For a variable force the work is the integral of F with respect to displacement: W = ∫_{x1}^{x2} F(x) dx.

questions.q: The dimension of work is the same as that of
questions.explanation: Work and energy both have dimensions [M L² T⁻²].

questions.q: A force of 10 N acts through a displacement of 2 m at an angle of 60° to the force. The work done is
A body of mass 2 kg moving at 4 m s⁻¹ has kinetic energy
A mass of 5 kg is raised through 2 m. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², the increase in gravitational potential energy is
A constant force of 20 N accelerates a body of mass 4 kg from rest through 5 m. The final kinetic energy of the body is
questions.explanation: By work-energy theorem W = F s = 20 × 5 = 100 J = ΔK (since K_i = 0).

questions.q: The power delivered by a force of 50 N that moves a body at a constant speed of 2 m s⁻¹ in the direction of the force is
A spring of spring constant 200 N m⁻¹ is stretched by 0.1 m. The elastic potential energy stored is
Which of the following forces is conservative?
questions.explanation: Gravitational force is conservative; work done by it is path-independent and a potential-energy function exists.

questions.q: A body falls freely from a height of 20 m. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², its kinetic energy just before hitting the ground is equal to its
questions.explanation: By conservation of mechanical energy, loss in PE = gain in KE, so K_final = m g h (taking U = 0 at ground).

questions.q: Two particles of equal mass m collide elastically in one dimension. If one was at rest, the velocities after collision are
options: the first stops and the second moves with the original speed of the first
questions.explanation: For equal masses in a 1-D elastic collision the velocities are exchanged: the moving particle stops and the stationary one acquires its velocity.

questions.q: A 2 kg object moving at 3 m s⁻¹ collides and sticks to a stationary 1 kg object. The common speed after collision is
questions.explanation: Momentum conservation: 2 × 3 = (2+1) v ⇒ 6 = 3 v ⇒ v = 2 m s⁻¹. Kinetic energy is not conserved (inelastic).

questions.q: The work done in stretching a spring of force constant k from extension x1 to x2 is
questions.explanation: W = ∫_{x1}^{x2} k x dx = ½ k (x2² − x1²).

questions.q: A machine lifts a load of 200 N through 5 m in 10 s. The power developed is
If the speed of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes
questions.explanation: K ∝ v², so doubling v multiplies K by four.

questions.q: The total mechanical energy of a system is conserved when
questions.explanation: Mechanical energy (K + U) is conserved if the work done by non-conservative forces is zero.

questions.q: A force F = (3x) N acts on a particle, where x is in metres. Work done in moving the particle from x = 0 to x = 2 m is
In a perfectly inelastic collision between two bodies, the coefficient of restitution is
questions.explanation: Coefficient of restitution e = 0 for a perfectly inelastic collision (the bodies stick together).

questions.q: A particle of mass 0.5 kg is moving with velocity 4 m s⁻¹. A constant force acts for 2 s and changes its velocity to 10 m s⁻¹ in the same direction. The work done by the force is
questions.explanation: ΔK = ½ × 0.5 × (100 − 16) = 0.25 × 84 = 21 J. By work-energy theorem this equals the work done.

questions.q: A body of mass m is projected vertically upward with speed u. The work done by gravity from projection to the highest point is
questions.explanation: At the highest point velocity is zero, so ΔK = −½ m u². Work done by gravity equals ΔK, hence W_g = −½ m u².

questions.q: Two masses m1 = 2 kg and m2 = 4 kg moving toward each other with speeds 3 m s⁻¹ and 1.5 m s⁻¹ respectively collide elastically in one dimension. The velocity of m1 after collision is
A block of mass 2 kg is dropped from a height of 5 m onto a spring of force constant 2000 N m⁻¹. The maximum compression of the spring is (g = 10 m s⁻²)
questions.explanation: Energy conservation: m g (h + x) = ½ k x². 2×10×(5+x) = ½×2000×x² ⇒ 20(5+x)=1000 x² ⇒ 5+x=50 x² ⇒ 50 x² − x − 5 = 0. Solving quadratic: x = [1 + √(1+1000)]/100 ≈ [1+√1001]/100 ≈ 0.2 m (positive root).

questions.q: A particle moves under a conservative force. If its potential energy decreases by 20 J, its kinetic energy
questions.explanation: For a conservative force, ΔK + ΔU = 0, so a decrease of 20 J in U produces an increase of 20 J in K.

questions.q: Two equal masses m moving with equal and opposite velocities u collide elastically. After collision their velocities are
options: each has velocity u in the original direction
they move perpendicular to the original line
questions.explanation: In a head-on elastic collision of equal masses the velocities are exchanged. Since they are equal and opposite, each reverses its direction and keeps the same speed.

questions.q: A constant power P is applied to a body of mass m initially at rest. The distance travelled by the body in time t is proportional to
questions.explanation: P = F v = m a v = m (dv/dt) v ⇒ P dt = m v dv. Integrating gives v ∝ √t, then s = ∫ v dt ∝ t^{3/2}.

questions.q: A 1 kg mass moving at 4 m s⁻¹ collides elastically with a stationary 3 kg mass. The speed of the 3 kg mass after collision is
The work done by all forces (conservative and non-conservative) on a system equals the change in
questions.explanation: By the work-energy theorem the total work done by every force equals the change in kinetic energy of the system, ΔK.
